title: Helping Family
description: A cap you can keep, the difference between a gift and a loan, and the cost of sending money.
wolfLine: Help from what remains. The rent is not a gift you can give.

lessons.title: Help Without Sinking
lessons.summary: A gift that spends the rent creates a second emergency.

steps.title: Your bills stay funded
steps.body:
Help is what you can give after rent and the [[emergency fund]] are covered.

Rent is **$1,400**. Other bills are **$1,100**. Income is **$3,000**. That leaves **$500** before any gift. A **$700** gift does not fit.

steps.prompt: Income is $3,000. Rent is $1,400 and other bills are $1,100. What is left before a gift?
A relative asks for $700. How far past that $500 is the ask?
Which gift fits this month?
choices: Up to $500, and only if the emergency fund is already intact
The $700, on a new credit card
steps.explain: The $500 is the room. Skipping rent or borrowing to donate creates the next crisis.

steps.prompt: If the need is family, the rent can wait.
steps.explain: Unpaid rent becomes your emergency. You cannot help for long from a place you are about to lose.

lessons.title: Gift or Loan
lessons.summary: Say which one it is before the money moves.

steps.context: A gift is gone on purpose. A loan has an amount and a date, in writing.

docs.title: A gift
docs.subtitle: You do not expect it back

steps.prompt: The loan is $200 a month until $2,000 is repaid. How many months is that?

docs.title: A gift
docs.subtitle: You do not expect it back

steps.prompt: You will be hurt if you never see the $2,000 again. Which page matches that?
why: A loan is the one you expect back.
A gift is money you have decided to lose.
The difference is whether you need it back.
steps.explain: If you need it back, it is a loan, and it needs a written amount and a date.

docs.title: A gift
docs.subtitle: You do not expect it back

steps.prompt: You can afford to lose $2,000, and you do not want to collect from your brother. Which page matches?
steps.explain: Call it a gift up front. A surprise loan is how holidays get ruined.

steps.prompt: Calling it a gift later, after they miss payments, is the same as agreeing up front.
steps.explain: The agreement has to exist when the money moves. A rewrite during a fight is not a plan.

steps.prompt: If you need the money back, write down the amount and the ___.
steps.explain: The date is what “back” means.

lessons.title: Co-signing
lessons.summary: Their loan becomes a loan you can be made to pay.

steps.title: You are not a reference
steps.body:
A [[co-signer|cosigner]] has to pay if the borrower does not. On this **$12,000** family loan, the payment is **$250** a month.

Three missed payments are **$750** already late. The other **$11,250** can still become yours too. “I only vouched” is not how the note reads.

steps.prompt: Three missed payments of $250. How much is already late?
The loan is $12,000 and $750 is late. How much of the original loan is not in those three payments?
steps.explain: $12,000 − $750 = $11,250. You can still be asked for that too.

steps.prompt: Who can the lender require to pay?
choices: You, the co-signer, for the whole loan if they do not pay
Only the relative who drives the car
Nobody, because it was a favor
steps.explain: The signature is the promise. A favor does not shrink it.

steps.prompt: Co-signing is safe if your credit score is higher than theirs.
steps.explain: Your good credit is why they asked. It is also what the missed payments can damage.

lessons.title: A Boundary
lessons.summary: Pick the number before the ask, not during it.

steps.title: A cap you chose on a calm day
steps.body:
Your cap is **$200** a month. An ask for **$500** is **$300** past it.

The boundary is the number you can say out loud. It is not a measure of how much you love someone.

steps.prompt: The ask is $500 and your cap is $200. How far over the cap is the ask?
You hold the cap for 6 months. How much have you given?
They ask again for $500, and the reason is urgent. What does a real boundary do?
choices: Stay at $200, and help in non-money ways past that
Become $500, because urgency deletes a cap
steps.explain: Urgency is when a pre-committed number earns its keep.

steps.prompt: A boundary means you never help.
steps.explain: It means the help has a size. $200 is still help.

lessons.title: Aging Parents
lessons.summary: Daily help is a wage, and Medicare is not the wallet for it.

steps.title: Price the hours
steps.body:
An aide at **$25** an hour, **8** hours a week, is **$200** a week. Across **4** weeks that is **$800** a month.

Medicare generally does not pay for long-term daily help at home. [[Medicaid]] may, if your parent qualifies. Rules differ by state. This is not a benefits decision. It is the price of the hours.

steps.prompt: What does $25 an hour for 8 hours cost?
What is that $200 week across 4 weeks?
What is that help for a year, at $800 a month?
Medicare generally pays for long-term daily help at home.
steps.explain: It generally does not. Medicaid may, if the person qualifies. Check the state program rather than assuming the hospital coverage continues at home.

lessons.title: Sending Money Abroad
lessons.summary: The fee is the line you see. The rate is the line people skip.

steps.title: Two costs
steps.body:
You want **$500** of value to arrive. This service adds a **$15** fee and an exchange rate that costs about **$20** more than a mid-market rate.

You pay **$535**. The cost of the service is **$35**, not $15.

doc.title: Money abroad

lines.label: Value you want them to receive

doc.note: The rate cost is how much less a mid-market rate would have taken.

steps.prompt: What do you pay on this receipt?

doc.title: Money abroad

lines.label: Value you want them to receive

doc.note: The rate cost is how much less a mid-market rate would have taken.

steps.prompt: What is the cost of the service, fee plus the rate?
You send this same transfer twice. What do the two fees and two rate costs add up to?
A service advertises “$0 fee” and a worse exchange rate. What do you compare?
choices: The amount they receive against what you paid
steps.explain: A $0 fee can hide a $20 rate. The test is what arrives, and what you paid to make it arrive.

lessons.title: Your Oxygen Mask
lessons.summary: You cannot send help from an account that cannot cover you.

steps.title: The order
steps.body:
Rent, food, and a small [[emergency fund]] come before a transfer to family.

This month those three need **$2,200**. Take-home pay is **$2,600**. The room for help is **$400**. Sending **$600** puts you **$200** underwater.

steps.prompt: Pay is $2,600 and your own floor is $2,200. How much room is there for help?
You send $600 anyway. How much short of your own floor are you?
Which order matches the oxygen mask?
choices: Your floor first, then help from what remains
Help first, then hope the rent can wait
Split the shortfall across two credit cards
steps.explain: The mask line is practical. A person who misses rent becomes the next person who needs help.

steps.prompt: Sending the $600 is fine if you plan to catch up next month.
steps.explain: Next month has its own floor. Starting it $200 behind is how the gap compounds.

lessons.title: Lina and Her Mom
lessons.summary: The number she can give is $200. Love does not add the other $100.

story.title: Lina and her mom
story.body:
Lina is 29. Take-home pay is **$3,200**. Rent is **$1,400**. Her other bills are **$1,600**. That is **$3,000** before she helps anyone, so **$200** is what the month has left.

Her mom needs **$300**. Sending it would leave Lina **$100** short of her own bills.

She tells her mom the truth: she can do **$200**, which is the whole remainder, or less if she wants any cushion. She does not put the last **$100** on a card.

steps.prompt: What do Lina’s rent and other bills add up to?
Take-home pay is $3,200. How much is left before any help?
If she sends $300, how short of her own bills is she?
Which amount keeps her bills paid?
choices: $300, plus a $100 card charge she will “figure out”
steps.explain: The month has $200 left. $300 spends bills she has already counted.

steps.prompt: Because the gap is only $100, the card is a harmless bridge.
steps.explain: The $100 is a debt, and next month’s $200 of room has to cover it before she can help again.

lessons.title: Sharpen Up
lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Helping Family
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: Pay is $2,800. Your floor is $2,400. How much can you give without cutting the floor?
You co-sign a $9,000 loan. They stop paying. Who can be collected from?
choices: Only the person who spent the money
The bank’s customer service line, and nobody else
steps.explain: A co-signer is responsible for the loan.

steps.prompt: An aide is $20 an hour for 10 hours. What is the week?
A “$0 fee” transfer cannot cost you anything.
steps.explain: The exchange rate can still take a cut. Compare what arrives with what you paid.
